newEntities.label: Circulating pyrophosphate
newEntities.description: Circulating calcification inhibitor measured in a human calciphylaxis registry; lower levels were associated with case status and outcomes, without establishing causal deficiency.

findings.subject: entity-pyrophosphate
findings.studySystem: Human calciphylaxis registry: 30 matched case-control pairs; 70-patient cohort, 67% ESKD. Fasting circulating PPi assay, predialysis in dialysis patients.
findings.text: Circulating pyrophosphate was lower in 30 patients with calciphylaxis than in 30 matched controls; lower PPi was associated with higher odds of calciphylaxis after adjustment for ALP, phosphate and BMI.
findings.quote: PPi levels were significantly lower among patients with calciphylaxis compared to matched controls
findings.quoteLocation: Main text, case-control results paragraph; table 1.
limitations: Small observational matched case-control study; measurement after diagnosis cannot establish temporal direction or causation.
Only 67% had ESKD; findings must not be treated as a dialysis-only population.
Industry funded, with several authors employed by the sponsor. No PPi-raising intervention was tested.

findings.subject: entity-pyrophosphate
findings.studySystem: Human calciphylaxis registry: 30 matched case-control pairs; 70-patient cohort, 67% ESKD. Fasting circulating PPi assay, predialysis in dialysis patients.
findings.text: In the calciphylaxis cohort, lower enrollment PPi was associated with higher short-term mortality; PPi also correlated with lesion count but not pain intensity. These observations do not establish that raising PPi improves outcomes.
findings.quote: At enrollment, PPi levels negatively correlated with the number of skin lesions
findings.quoteLocation: Main text, cohort severity and mortality results paragraph.
limitations: Seventy-patient cohort, short follow-up, substantial within-person PPi variability and possible residual confounding.
The adjusted mortality association was reported in the ESKD subgroup; no universal mortality effect is asserted.
No significant association with pain intensity; biomarker association does not demonstrate treatment benefit.
findings.distinctFindingRationale: Separate cohort outcome finding, rather than counting the matched case-control comparison as an independent replication.
